raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Mooncake Prefill decodes registration metadata from a peer-controlled packed-list frame. The list count was trusted before validating the frame or comparing it with the local model layout. As reported in #45012, a 400,004-byte frame can declare 100,000 empty child buffers, causing Python to materialize and retain 100,000 lists for one fake Decode session.

This PR addresses that parser-amplification vector. It intentionally does not claim to add peer authentication or a global peer-table policy.

## Modifications

- Validate packed-list headers, length tables, payload totals, and integer element alignment before decoding.
- Add optional list-count bounds to the shared wire decoder.
- Bound Mooncake registration state lists by the local model state-component count before creating any child lists.
- Convert malformed registration metadata into a dropped peer registration instead of letting the bootstrap receive thread exit.

## Accuracy Tests

Added CPU regression coverage to `test_disaggregation_wire.py` for:

- the reported 100,000-list amplification frame;
- truncated headers and length tables;
- declared/actual payload mismatches;
- integer-width misalignment;
- valid empty-state registration metadata.

Local focused validation:

```text
amplification frame rejected before list materialization: PASS (peak=445 bytes)
valid/malformed wire matrix: PASS
bootstrap parse boundary survives malformed registration: PASS
```

Also passed:

```text
python3 -m py_compile <3 changed Python files>
isort 7.0.0 --check-only <3 changed files>
ruff 0.15.1 check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037 <3 changed files>
ruff 0.15.1 format --check <3 changed files>
git diff --check
```

The local host does not have the project PyTorch test environment, so the registered CPU test file was not executed end to end locally; the exact changed functions were exercised directly without importing the GPU/runtime stack.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. The new checks execute only while decoding bootstrap/registration metadata, outside model forward execution. The rejected attack frame now fails after reading its 4-byte count instead of unpacking and allocating 100,000 child entries.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the contribution guide.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation. N/A: no public API or configuration change.
- [x] Provide model accuracy/speed benchmarks. N/A: this is a bootstrap wire-validation fix; focused CPU mechanism results are above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

Refs #45012
